description:
FILED s440 from agent D's #501 report (recorded in ir-spec sec. 5.4). Fix costs a per-sort runtime check (resolve the NAME once at sort entry through %p-resolve-sub-symbol; an unresolvable name -> %p-call-of-undefined-sub's die, even for a 0/1-element list). Bar: `sort nonexistent (7)` / `()` / `(1,2)` vs perl (all die), `sort by_num (7)` unchanged, AUTOLOAD comparator (perl #30661) unchanged; a row in Pl/t/sort-01.t.

DONE (s446j, agent J).  perl resolves a named comparator at sort ENTRY and dies "Undefined sort subroutine \"main::nm\" called" even when the list is EMPTY or one element long, and it dies AFTER the LIST's own side effects (probed with $|=1: the list's prints come first).  That ordering is why the check could not go where the comparator lambda is BUILT -- that form is an ARGUMENT, evaluated before the list.  Shape: `sort NAME LIST` now emits (p-sort-named 'pl-NAME (p-sort-cmp ...)), a p-named-cmp struct carrying the symbol, and p-sort resolves it (%p-sort-resolve-comparator) on entry.  The check asks "a BODY or the package's own AUTOLOAD" -- never fboundp alone: perl reaches AUTOLOAD for a comparator (perl #30661, probed at both list sizes), and a forward declaration with no body dies.  Both halves of that question are now ONE reading each: %p-sub-has-body-p and %p-autoload-symbol, extracted from %p-call-of-undefined-sub and routed through its three other copies (p-backslash-sub x2, the package sub scan).
A SECOND BUG FELL OUT and had to be fixed in the same commit (#550's sibling, recorded there): perl-tests/sort.t:240 spells `sort main'Backwards` with the PERL-4 tick separator, and cl_name emitted `pl-main'Backwards` -- where `'` is the CL reader's QUOTE and terminates the token.  In call position that read as (pl-main 'Backwards) (an undefined sub -- silently wrong since forever); in the new QUOTED position it became two arguments and the eval died "invalid number of arguments: 3".  cl_name now rewrites `'` before a word character to `::`, which is perl's own toker rule and the one the runtime already applies to symbolic names (%p-tick-package-seps).  sort.t is back to 204/0 and the row now runs for real.  Guards: Pl/t/sort-01.t rows 22-23 (entry resolution at three list sizes + AUTOLOAD + fwd-decl; the LIST runs before the die) and row 21's message expectation updated to perl's own sort-specific diagnostic.
subject: `sort NAME LIST` resolves the comparator LATE: perl resolves the sort sub on ENTRY (`sort nonexistent (7)` and even `sort nonexistent ()` die although the comparator never runs); PCL resolves at the first comparison, so both succeed -- die-TIMING, not value
